item.title: Operations Research and Data-Driven Decision Making for Complex Socio-Economic Systems in Ibero-America: Evidence and Applications
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks research that applies operations research and data-driven methodologies to address complex socio-economic challenges within Ibero-American countries. The focus is on demonstrating how quantitative and analytical approaches can inform policy decisions and solve real-world problems affecting social and economic systems in this region.

item.title: Collaborative Intelligence in Operations Research: Models, Methods, and Applications
item.content:encoded:
Olga Battaïa, Kedge Business School

Yasser Dessouky, San Jose State University

Reza Zanjirani Farahani, Paris School of Business

Masood Fathi, University of Skövde

Madjid Tavana, La Salle University

Modern operations research increasingly demands approaches that combine human expertise with artificial intelligence and distributed problem-solving capabilities. This special issue seeks research that explores how collaborative intelligence—the synergy between human decision-makers, AI-driven systems, and mathematical optimization—can address the complexity, uncertainty, and dynamic nature of contemporary operational challenges.

The issue welcomes contributions spanning theoretical models, computational algorithms, and practical applications that demonstrate how human-AI collaboration, multi-agent coordination, decentralized optimization, and machine learning can enhance decision-making and system resilience. Submissions should showcase both rigorous mathematical foundations and real-world relevance, emphasizing the transformative potential of collaborative approaches in logistics, production, service systems, emergency response, and other complex operational environments.

item.title: Data-Driven Reliability Modeling and Decision Support in Industrial Engineering Systems
item.content:encoded:
Yi-Kuei Lin, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

This special issue seeks contributions on data-driven and intelligent approaches to reliability modeling for industrial engineering systems, including manufacturing, supply chains, logistics, energy, transportation, and service operations. The growing availability of operational and condition-monitoring data has created opportunities to complement traditional probabilistic and stochastic reliability methods with machine learning and statistical learning techniques.

The issue emphasizes the integration of reliability modeling with decision support frameworks, enabling practitioners to move beyond reliability assessment toward actionable, reliability-informed decisions under uncertainty. Both theoretical developments and practical applications are welcome, with particular interest in papers demonstrating methodological rigor and real-world industrial relevance.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Data Science
item.content:encoded:
Dries F. Benoit, Ghent University

Kristof Coussement, Institut d'Economie Scientifique Et de Gestion

Cem İyigün, Middle East Technical University

Asil Oztekin, University of Massachusetts Lowell

This special section seeks papers that advance both theoretical and practical contributions to data science and predictive analytics. The focus is on demonstrating how new techniques create organizational value and may require changes in business processes. The work bridges operations research with analytics, treating analytics as an organizational discipline that leverages both data science and OR methodologies.

The section invites researchers and practitioners to explore multiple dimensions of analytics: ethical and governance challenges in data collection and behavioral influence; applications and limitations of OR techniques with big data and distributed systems; organizational barriers to analytics adoption and real-time OR applications; methods for data quality, hypothesis testing, and integration of unstructured data; and how visualization and problem structuring enhance analytics projects.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Global Supply Chain Reconfiguration Under Tariff Uncertainty
item.content:encoded:
Jiaguo Liu, Dalian Maritime University

Hakan Yildiz, Wayne State University

Guoqing Zhang, University of Windsor

Global supply chains face mounting pressures from tariff uncertainty and shifting trade policies, requiring urgent reconfiguration of sourcing strategies, manufacturing locations, and logistics networks. The current environment presents unprecedented complexity with high tariff rates, retaliatory measures, and escalating trade tensions creating significant practical challenges.

This special issue seeks high-quality research applying Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence methods to address supply chain reconfiguration challenges under tariff uncertainty. The journal welcomes theoretical developments, methodological innovations, applied modeling studies, and interdisciplinary work integrating OR, AI, supply chain management, and international economics with real-world case applications.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming: Artificial Intelligence for Decision Making in Economic and Social Sciences
item.content:encoded:
Matteo Rocca, University of Insubria

Davide La Torre, Skema Business School

Constantin Zopounidis, Technical University of Crete

This special issue seeks papers that integrate multiple objective programming, goal programming, and artificial intelligence to address complex decision-making in economic and social sciences. The issue welcomes both substantially extended papers from the 16th International Conference on Multiple Objective Programming and Goal Programming (MOPGP'25) held in Varese, Italy, and original work not previously presented at the conference.

Multiple objective optimization and goal programming provide structured frameworks for evaluating conflicting objectives, while artificial intelligence enhances these approaches through data analytics and machine learning. The combination enables processing of large datasets and improves the accuracy and robustness of decision models and predictions in addressing real-world challenges.

item.title: OR for Sustainability in Supply Chain Management
item.content:encoded:
Kannan Govindan, University of Southern Denmark

Organizations must align operations with UN sustainable development goals to address resource depletion and environmental degradation. This special section seeks research using operations research methods to implement SDGs in supply chain management, particularly advanced optimization techniques like multi-attribute and multi-objective decision-making.

The section invites contributions on three themes: designing sustainable policies with stakeholder involvement, implementing SDGs through innovative supply chain practices, and monitoring progress toward sustainability targets in supply chain governance. Research should examine how organizations balance economic growth with resource conservation and environmental protection.

The collection welcomes interdisciplinary approaches integrating environmental, economic, and social perspectives. Submissions should demonstrate how operations research and optimization algorithms support data-driven decisions that achieve sustainable development goals while improving organizational efficiency and human wellbeing.

item.title: OR in Medicine and Health Care
item.content:encoded:
Eva K. Lee, Georgia Institute of Technology

Ariela Sofer, George Mason University

This special section seeks contributions applying optimization and computational methods to medical and healthcare challenges. The collection welcomes theoretical and methodological work on models and algorithms including continuous linear and nonlinear optimization, integer programming, combinatorial optimization, and stochastic approaches applied to medical and biological problems. Applications span disease modeling, diagnosis, treatment planning, imaging, epidemiology, and molecular biology.

The partnership between mathematical programming researchers and medical professionals—clinicians, biologists, public health officials—creates opportunities to advance both optimization theory and practice while addressing important healthcare problems. The special section, established in 2000, publishes state-of-the-art research in this dynamic field on an ongoing basis.

Original, previously unpublished manuscripts submitted to this collection are evaluated through standard peer review by the Annals of Operations Research.

Appel publié par Annals of Operations Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
